discussion:
## Remove iptables-persistent Package

The `iptables-persistent` package can be removed with the following command:

```
$ apt-get remove iptables-persistent
```

**Rationale:**

Running both `ufw` and the services included in the
`iptables-persistent` package may lead to conflict.

steps.name: Remove iptables-persistent Package
steps.shell:
# Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms
if dpkg-query --show --showformat='${db:Status-Status}' 'ufw' 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^installed$'; then

# CAUTION: This remediation script will remove iptables-persistent
# from the system, and may remove any packages
# that depend on iptables-persistent. Execute this
# remediation AFTER testing on a non-production
# system!


# check wether the package is virtual: if not, remove it.
# if the package is virtual, iterate on providers
#  if a provider is installed, remove it
is_virtual=`apt-cache showpkg "iptables-persistent" | grep -Pzc 'Versions: \n\n'`
if [ $is_virtual = 1 ]; then
    rprovides_line=`apt-cache showpkg "iptables-persistent" | grep -n 'Reverse Provides:' | cut -f1 -d:`
    pkglist=`apt-cache showpkg "iptables-persistent" | tail -n +$(($rprovides_line + 1)) | cut -f1 -d' '`
    for package in $pkglist; do
        not_installed=`apt-cache policy $package | grep -c 'Installed: (none)'`
	if [ $not_installed = 0 ]; then
	    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=60 remove -y $package
	fi
    done
else
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=60 remove -y "iptables-persistent"
fi

else
    >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done'
fi
